faq.q: Is the wind really stronger at sea?
faq.a: Usually, yes. With no hills or buildings in the way, wind over the sea is faster and less gusty than over nearby land, so offshore turbines run nearer their full power more of the time.
asks: Why is it windier at sea?

faq.q: Why does a little more wind give much more power?
faq.a: The power in wind depends on its speed cubed: twice the speed means two times two times two, eight times the power. So a site with slightly faster wind makes much more electricity.
asks: What is the cube rule for wind?

faq.q: How do they build turbines at sea?
faq.a: Special jack-up ships stand on legs on the seabed to make a steady platform. Cranes lift the tower, nacelle and blades onto a foundation, often a giant steel tube hammered into the seabed called a monopile.

In deep water, where fixed foundations cannot reach the seabed, turbines can stand on floating platforms held by anchor cables. Hywind Scotland, opened in 2017, was the world's first floating wind farm.

faq.q: How does electricity get back from an offshore wind farm?
faq.a: Cables from each turbine join at an offshore substation, which raises the voltage. A thick export cable buried in the seabed then carries the power to shore.
asks: How is offshore wind power brought ashore?

facts: Offshore wind farms typically produce around 40 percent of their maximum possible output over a year, more than most onshore wind farms.
Hywind Scotland, opened in 2017, was the world's first floating offshore wind farm.

quiz.say: If the wind speed doubles, roughly how much more power can a turbine get from it?
quiz.show: Wind speed doubles: power goes up by…
quiz.why: Power in the wind goes with speed cubed, and two cubed is eight.

wrong.1: Power does not simply follow speed; it rises with the cube.
wrong.2: Four would be speed squared; wind power goes with the cube.
